title: GAL-VNE: Solving the VNE Problem with Global Reinforcement Learning and Local One-Shot Neural Prediction

problem.claim: The VNE problem is an NP-hard combinatorial problem of finding node and edge mappings between a virtual network request and a physical network resource.

gap.claim: Existing learning-based methods are hindered by inefficient, poorly scalable autoregressive mapping and by independently treating online requests, which limits long-term service performance.

contributions.claim: GAL-VNE uses a synergistic global-and-local learning approach for VNE.

At the global level, reinforcement learning captures cross-request relations for resource accommodation; at the local level, one-shot solution generation replaces sequential node-by-node decision-making.

Within a rank-then-search paradigm, a GNN-based node ranker is pretrained with imitation supervision from an off-the-shelf solver and neighboring smooth regularization, then finetuned with reinforcement learning against business objectives such as revenue and cost.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmarks reportedly show that GAL-VNE outperforms classic and learning-based methods in efficacy and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: VNE is an NP-hard virtual-to-physical network mapping problem.
Learning-based approaches face efficiency, scalability, and long-term online-service limitations.
GAL-VNE combines global reinforcement learning across requests with local one-shot prediction within each request.
The method uses a rank-then-search pipeline with GNN pretraining, smoothness regularization, and reinforcement-learning finetuning against business objectives.
Benchmark experiments reportedly show gains over classic and learning-based methods in efficacy and efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The method combines imitation supervision from a moderately expensive solver with reinforcement-learning finetuning against final business objectives.

interpretation.claim: A staged training strategy can use solver quality to initialize prediction while later aligning the model with nondifferentiable operational objectives.

application.claim: When direct optimization is difficult, use an existing solver for pretraining and policy optimization for objective alignment.

exception.claim: This approach depends on access to a sufficiently useful solver and does not remove the stated challenge of encoding constraints end to end.
